title: Driving to Boston to hear Domino
summary: Puzzled by how easy he was to book, Thomas drives to Boston, finds a New Orleans band and screaming fans, and predicts Domino will be as big as Fats Waller.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And I said to myself... I booked him for the first week so fast, I said, "Let me go up to Boston and hear this son-of-a-gun, because something's wrong. I ain't never had nobody that easy to book." He was only making $350 or $400 a night. So I...
For him or for the band?
For the band. That's all them Rock-and-Rollers made in (?). But they had a percentage deal going off the door, where if they were getting $350 over the door amount they got 50 percent...
If I booked them for $350, over $700 he got 50 percent.
If he got over $700 on the door?
Yeah. And then he got 50 percent over the old rate.
Yeah. If he went to, say, $2,000, he'd come out of it with $1,000. And he had been hitting percentages anyway.

So something told me to go up to Boston and see him. Because I couldn't understand how the guy was so easy to book. Because I had booked him all of them Mondays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays and Thursdays... So I got in my car, and drove up to Boston. And I'll always remember I slid down that last hill, because that's before they had a turnpike. I got there, oh, about 11 o'clock.

And I got the biggest shock of my life. This cat had all New Orleans musicians, and they was... That music... Without him singing, they was playin' up a breeze. And then when he come on at intermission, the girls just swarmed around him. And he didn't write too good... Now, he was an autograph freak. He'd autograph, he'd write the (?) name. But they just wanted to shake his hand and kiss him on the cheek, just to get close to him. I didn't know he was that big!

And in Boston, you see, you've got a mixed group of people up there. You've got the White, the Black, the Portuguese -- and they all go to the dance. It don't make any difference. If there's something good they want to see, they go. Remember when we used to play that place up there that had the...that (?) thing?
So when I went up to see him, once I saw and heard that band, then I saw why he was so good. And he had all these

songs going; he had about two or three records going then. So I came back to the office that Monday. And we always had a meeting on Tuesday. And I couldn't wait. I couldn't wait til Tuesday come for me to report on Domino. So I came in, and I said... I made a statement. I said, "One day Domino will be as big as Fats Waller." Man, everybody laughed at me! Even Billy Shaw laughed at me. But I was just makin' them what I thought! But I've always been like that. Whatever is on my mind... If I see an artist and I think he's got some talent, I say it. And that made me make up my mind. I said, "I'm gonna do everything I can for this son-of-a-gun." And I booked him all in good places.
